rec.name: Collection Page Type Badges (Product Card Attribute Pill)
rec.status: Built — delivered, documented (Slite doc + setup video); in Sectionfy theme under Theme settings > Collections

what.text: A full-width pill-shaped badge under each product card on collection pages (below title, price and ratings). It shows a short attribute or benefit such as 'dry skin' with an icon, or 'oily skin' with an icon. The content comes from a product metafield, so each product can show a different badge. Colors, corner radius and alignment are set globally in theme settings.

why.text: Shoppers scanning a grid can't open every product. A visible 'who it's for' or 'use case' label (skin type, evening routine) lets them self-qualify in seconds. This cuts decision effort and the number of PDP visits needed to compare, and sends the right shoppers to the right product. The icon adds quick visual recognition, and the soft pill style adds emphasis without competing with price or the CTA.

how.text: 1) In snippet product-item.liquid, paste the badge block at the end of the product-item__info div. It renders only if the 'show_cro_type_badges' setting is on and the metafield is not blank. It outputs a wrapper div containing a flex span styled from the theme settings. 2) In settings_schema.json, add a 'CRO | Type Badges' group at the end of the 'Collections' settings: checkbox, SVG color, text color, background, border-radius range 0-100px (step 4, default 100), and alignment select (Left/Center/Right). 3) Create a multi-line text product metafield 'CRO | Type Badges' with namespace and key standard.cro_type_badges. It accepts HTML, SVG or plain text, and an tag for an image icon. Put the icon and text together in one metafield, so no extra metafield per icon is needed.

items: Per-product content via metafield standard.cro_type_badges (text, inline SVG or tag)

dependencies.text: Product metafield definition standard.cro_type_badges (multi-line text). Requires edits to the theme's product-item.liquid snippet and settings_schema.json. It uses the CSS variable --base-font-size, so the theme must define it. It was built as a theme-level feature (Theme settings > Collections), not a standalone section with blocks. No third-party app is needed. The ticket asked for a 'Section', but the code is a theme-settings feature. Icon position (left/right of the text) is not separately configurable in the delivered code; it depends on the HTML in the metafield (I).
